updated: 30 October 2026 · playable review candidate / four visual iterations
verdict: Playable review candidate · reference benchmark not passed

pieces.name: The 1,000-floor campaign
pieces.evidence: Finite completion, seeded content, real hazard contact and recoverable checkpoints. Four independent campaign reviews corrected persistence defects; no remaining P1 was found in the final bounded review. The policy follows one route per floor.

pieces.name: Character & living tower
pieces.evidence: Original articulated explorer and companion; ten district themes, textured architecture and connected cliff terraces. The sampled late-landing camera defect is corrected. ASTRO BOT remains the preferred visual reference.

pieces.name: Viewer controls & saves
pieces.evidence: All six Chromium functional checks pass in the supported low-quality mode. High-quality captures have no page errors, but this headless host is slow; hardware frame-rate and long-duration operation remain unverified.

iterations.label: Baseline · d1678cd
iterations.title: From a catalogue entry to a real expedition
iterations.summary: The existing repository named AI vs 1,000 Floors and specified a finite campaign with checkpoints, but had no playable Game 4 runtime. This is the honest starting point.
iterations.verdict: No visual benchmark result is claimed. First runtime and captures are being prepared.

iterations.label: Iteration 1 · actual gameplay
iterations.title: A working climb, an honest first comparison
iterations.summary: The first real 3D campaign introduced an explorer, companion, seeded platforms, timed hazards and checkpoint progress. The independent critic inspected actual frames and moving traversal beside official ASTRO BOT clips.
iterations.verdict: Reference preferred. Main gaps: floating primitive scenery, weak material distinction, limited articulation, hazard clarity and portrait framing.

iterations.label: Iteration 2 · actual gameplay
iterations.title: Stronger platform dressing and a clearer portrait HUD
iterations.summary: Added terracotta edging, vegetation, movement interpolation and a low exit beacon; compressed the mobile HUD. Campaign reviews corrected live hazard contact and accepted-save inconsistencies.
iterations.verdict: Benchmark remains not passed. The scene still needs authored depth, stronger character animation, safe camera framing and fewer draw calls.

iterations.label: Iteration 3 · actual gameplay
iterations.title: An articulated explorer in a more developed tower
iterations.summary: Added a skinned character with expressive joint poses, layered materials, botanical architecture and static geometry batching. Portrait framing improved; a fresh moving review found an upcoming exit entering view too late.
iterations.verdict: Reference preferred. The critic returned late landing visibility and thin environmental context for another build.

iterations.label: Iteration 4 · inspected review candidate
iterations.title: A connected world, with the next landing in view
iterations.summary: Added terraced cliff islands, lower galleries and distant settlements. The camera uses the real route cursor, anticipates the following landing and keeps a stable scale. Actual captures include floors 006, 102, 403 and 902. The clip is a compressed recording from a slow software-rendered session; it does not establish hardware frame rate.
iterations.verdict: The fresh critic no longer reproduced the earlier exit clipping in sampled floor-004 traversal. The benchmark remains not passed: district composition, surface finish and expressive motion still trail the reference.

references.name: ASTRO BOT
references.role: Primary: fully realized characters, animation, environments, camera clarity and feedback. Actual Spring-Loaded Run and Rising Heat gameplay clips are the comparison sources.

references.name: Luigi’s Mansion 3
references.role: Distinct floor identities through architecture, dressing, staging and light.

references.name: Returnal · Tower of Sisyphus
references.role: Tower presentation, spatial depth and readable action.

gaps: The fixed ASTRO BOT gameplay reference remains preferred; improvements to this build do not constitute a benchmark win.
Districts need more distinct large-scale composition and surface treatment; repeated square platforms and brick towers remain prominent.
The campaign has one generated route per floor. Alternative route selection remains an explicit design gap.
High-quality motion was slow on this shared headless graphics host. Real-hardware frame-rate, audio listening quality and broader accessibility review remain open.
The ten-district resource cycle returned to its exact initial geometry/texture counts; a long production soak and live audience operation have not been established.
